recognize_zh: 箭頭所指紅血球的血紅素被推擠到一側，另一側只剩透明薄膜像水泡（blister cell／偏心細胞），背景還有多個咬痕狀與濃縮變形的紅血球及一個嗜多色性紅血球，符合 G6PD 缺乏症的氧化性溶血。
features: Blister cells: hemoglobin condensed to one side with a clear, membrane-bound peripheral vacuole (arrows)
Eccentrocytes and irregularly contracted, densely staining red cells
Bite-like cells with notched or flattened margins
Polychromatophilic red cell indicating reticulocyte response (small arrow)
Adequate platelets; no agglutination or schistocyte-dominant pattern
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous red cells with hemoglobin retracted to one side leaving a clear, membrane-lined peripheral space (blister cells/eccentrocytes), together with bite-like and irregularly contracted dense cells. A polychromatophilic red cell indicates a reticulocyte response. Platelets are adequate and no red cell agglutination is seen. Findings are consistent with acute oxidant hemolysis, as seen in G6PD deficiency; a supravital stain for Heinz bodies and a G6PD assay performed after recovery are recommended.

ddx.vs: Spherocytes are round, uniformly dense cells lacking the eccentric clear membrane pocket of blister cells.
MAHA shows sharp-edged schistocytes and helmet cells with thrombocytopenia rather than hemoglobin retracted from an intact membrane.
Unstable hemoglobins also produce Heinz bodies and bite cells, so a normal G6PD assay with a positive isopropanol stability test and Hb analysis separate them.
Artifactual refractile holes occur in many cells in one area with sharp edges and no associated bite cells or polychromasia.
